title: Edge Site Networking Requirements and Risk Log
summary: Field notes from feasibility call and rack survey focused on network topology, controlled media transfer, and cryptographic keying for an air-gapped POC. Emphasizes constraints around DNS, NTP, and egress; proposes mitigations and a minimal on-prem runbook to unblock a 2-rack pilot.
objectives: Capture concrete network and operational constraints at customer site
Identify minimum hardware and software footprint for POC (2 racks)
Define secure artifact transfer and image signing workflow for air-gapped bootstrap
List hard blockers vs. mitigations and owner for each action item
hardware_inventory: 2x racks for POC (customer-provided) - target: 3U per rack for Redwood nodes
Compute: 2x servers/rack, spec: 1x AMD 7742 or 2x Intel 6338/48 cores (customer to confirm)
GPU: customer to provide 2x A10G-equivalent per server OR dedicated GPU shelf (optional)
Storage: 4x NVMe per server (1.6TB), RAID not required for POC but local LUKS recommended
Switching: 1x Top-of-Rack L2+ switch with 10G uplinks, STP disabled recommended for test
Firewall / Edge: Palo Alto PA or equivalent (customer uses Palo Alto PA-440), must support static NAT and port ACLs
Jumpbox: 1 hardened bastion host for maintenance with two-factor auth (customer will provision)
HSM / KMS: customer has Thales nShield on main site; remote HSM not available in air-gapped zone
network_constraints: No direct outbound internet from racks in air-gapped zone
DNS requests must be answered by internal resolvers only; no external resolution allowed
NTP access is blocked outbound; time sync must be provided via internal GPS/Stratum server
Strict egress filtering, only approved ports allowed via perimeter firewall
No DHCP on production VLANs; customer uses static addressing for racks
Proxying allowed through a validated jumpbox only. TLS termination must happen at the control plane inside air-gapped zone
MTU differences observed between core (9000) and ToR (1500) — may impact large packet transfers/rsync
No multicast/broadcast spanning between racks due to segmentation policies
security_controls_required: Control plane and runtime must use mTLS with customer CA
Disk encryption at-rest (LUKS) for all local volumes
Image and artifact signing mandatory: vendor-signed ISOs + SHA256 manifest
HSM-backed key storage preferred; if not available, use customer-managed KMS with strict access policies
Audit logging to local SIEM collector (forwarding via secure courier if external SIEM unreachable)
RBAC enforced for cluster admin actions; local AD/LDAP integration required
Supply chain verification for docker images and binaries before airgap transfer
software_dependencies: Redwood private runtime v0.9.x (airgap-compatible bundle required)
Container runtime: containerd 1.6.x pinned in POC
OS baseline: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (customer preferred) with kernel >=5.15
Transport tools: rsync 3.2.x and signed tarball ingestion tool (redwood-artifact-ingest)
Key tooling: openssl 3.x, cosign for signatures, optional yubikey-agent for offline signing
Monitoring: Prometheus (local scrape), Grafana (local), logs shipped to local Elastic or Splunk instance
findings: Customer cannot provide outbound internet in the air-gapped room — requires fully offline bootstrap
On-site HSM is only available in main data center; air-gapped racks have no HSM access — KMS proxy required
Customer security team requires image signing and validation before import; they will run signatures in a vetted DMZ
Bandwith between main site and air-gapped floor is limited to 200 Mbps and scheduled windows only
Customer is willing to provide a locked USB transfer protocol and courier chain for initial images but needs a documented chain-of-custody
NTP provider must be local; customer committed to standing up a Stratum server for POC

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Artifact corruption during offline transfer. Mitigation: double-signed tarballs, SHA256 verification, checksum recorded at handoff
Risk: Time skew due to no external NTP. Mitigation: require local Stratum server + hardware RTC sync and pre-checks in runbook
Risk: Lack of HSM in zone exposing keys. Mitigation: short-lived keys provisioned via KMS proxy with strict ACL and auditing
Risk: MTU mismatch causing failed gRPC streams. Mitigation: test flows with 1500 MTU first; enable path MTU discovery and provide fallback treadmill
Risk: Unexpected firewall policies blocking control plane. Mitigation: provide minimal port/URL matrix and request temporary opens for bootstrap with audit
notes: Meeting notes (raw): customer security is conservative — insisted on airgap transfer via signed USBs and escort. They will not allow us to bring any external drive; instead they will receive sealed media from our logistics partner. Unresolved Qs: (1) Can customer provide a local HSM or will they accept KMS proxy? (2) Who owns the chain-of-custody documentation at handoff? (3) Is temporary egress for package validation in DMZ acceptable? Action: follow up with Field Ops and Security to finalize transfer pattern. See slack thread #onprem-airgap for more context. Related tickets: SE-2219, OPS-640. Quick win: prepare an image manifest template and signature checklist to hand to customer at next workshop.
